title: Flight booking service and strategies
idea: The core design is one FlightBookingService that runs hold and pay, and reaches fare inventory, pricing and payment only through injected interfaces.

analogy.text: A travel agent at a desk. The agent follows one script, but phones the airline for seats, checks the price sheet, and swipes the card.
analogy.breaks: A real agent improvises when a call fails; the service only follows code.

points: FlightBookingService is a facade: callers see only `hold` and `pay`.
`FareInventory` hides where seat counts live: a map now, PostgreSQL later.
`PricingStrategy` is the strategy pattern: each pricing rule is its own class.
`PaymentGateway` and `Clock` are injected, so tests control money and time.

steps.caption: Asha asks to hold two Y-SAVER seats on AI-101.
The service looks up the fare and reads how many seats are left.
The inventory reserves two seats from the count, or refuses the whole request.
The pricing strategy prices one passenger; the service multiplies by two and freezes the total.
The caller gets PNR-1, HELD, with a deadline from the injected `Clock`.
Another request for two more seats finds one left. Nothing is reserved.
Asha pays before the deadline. The gateway charges the frozen total once.
The service issues one Ticket per passenger and returns the TICKETED booking.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: The core flow with every collaborator passed into the constructor. Types are trimmed versions of page 2; the payment gateway is a lambda that always approves. Status is trimmed to HELD and TICKETED here; page 4 adds CONFIRMED between them.

walk.text: A fixed `Clock`, one flight, and an inventory loaded with three seats.
Wire the service with one implementation of each interface.
Hold two seats, print what is left, then try two more and get refused.
Three interfaces: inventory, pricing, payment. Each one is a swap point.
`reserve` refuses unless enough seats remain; it is not thread-safe yet.
`hold` reserves seats, prices them, and stamps a 15-minute deadline.
`pay` checks the hold is live, charges once, then issues one ticket per passenger.

code.title: A new pricing strategy
code.caption: Scarcity pricing added as a new class. The service and the fixed strategy stay untouched.

walk.text: Tiers: 20 percent extra at five or fewer seats, 50 at two or fewer.
Price one passenger under both strategies as seats run out.
The new class copies its tiers into a sorted map.
`ceilingEntry` finds the tightest tier that applies; integer math keeps money exact.

pitfalls: Do not add `if (fewSeatsLeft)` branches to the service; write a new strategy.
Freeze the total at hold time, or the traveller pays a price never shown.
Never call `Instant.now()` inside the service; inject a `Clock`.

quiz.q: What does NewPricingRule print for 3 seats left?
quiz.why: The smallest tier key at or above 3 is 5, which adds 20 percent. 450000 times 120 over 100 is 540000; the fixed strategy ignores seats left.

takeaway: One facade service; every rule that changes sits behind an injected interface.

starters: Should the price be computed before or after reserving seats?
How would I test FlightBookingService with a gateway that declines?
When would a decorator fit better than a new strategy here?
